AuthContext.tsx:424-436 refreshTokenInternal reads `const storedUser = tokenStorage.getUser()` and only calls setUser inside `if (storedUser)` — cold-boot init routes through this path (line 481 `await refreshTokenInternal()`) so if USER_KEY was cleared/corrupted (getUser returns null on JSON.parse throw, line 152-159) but the refresh token is valid, the API refresh succeeds, new tokens are written to storage, but React `user` state stays null → isAuthenticated=false and the user is stuck on /login with freshly-rotated tokens (silently invalidating whatever session the next login creates).

lib/api.ts:89 lists 429 in RETRYABLE_STATUS_CODES and the response-interceptor retry loop (lib/api.ts:276-300) computes delay via `calculateRetryDelay(retryCount)` (1s/2s/4s + jitter) with zero reference to `Retry-After` — grep for 'retry-after' in api.ts returns no matches. On a 429 the server's back-pressure hint (e.g. `Retry-After: 60`) is discarded and the client hammers the endpoint ~3 times in <10s; errorHandler.ts:335 already has a `parseRetryAfter` helper the retry loop doesn't consult.

lib/api.ts:370 `export default getApiClient();` is evaluated at module import time, before AuthProvider's effect calls `configureApiClient({ getToken, onUnauthorized })` (AuthContext.tsx:380-383). That initial call creates an unconfigured axios instance (no token getter, no 401 handler) and freezes it as the module default; a later `configureApiClient` replaces the module-level `apiInstance` but the default export still references the original. Today no importer uses the default (grep confirms only named `getApiClient`/`configureApiClient` are used), but the export is a live footgun — any future `import api from '../lib/api'` will silently send requests without Authorization and never trigger silent refresh on 401.
